process holding the domain file descriptor across a rebind can
therefore fault in an arbitrary physical page with read/write
access, ignoring the entry permissions.

Additionally, since the domain file mmap lacks VM_IO, the domain
file itself can be mapped and passed to vhost_vdpa_va_map(),
producing self-referential entries that bypass the coherent path
check.

To fix, only translate entries whose backing file is the domain
file itself in vduse_domain_get_coherent_page(), reject such
entries in vduse_domain_set_map() since only external mappings
should be imported, and set VM_IO on the domain file mmap so
vhost_vdpa_va_map() refuses to map it in the first place.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: virtio_blk: use synchronous quiesce in virtblk_freeze_priv() blk_mq_run_work_fn() can call…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

virtio_blk: use synchronous quiesce in virtblk_freeze_priv()

blk_mq_run_work_fn() can call blk_mq_sched_dispatch_requests() through
blk_mq_run_dispatch_ops(). The dispatcher checks QUEUE_FLAG_QUIESCED
while the flag is clear. It can then be preempted before it gets a
request. At that time, it has no queue usage reference, so
blk_mq_freeze_queue() does not wait for it.

virtblk_freeze_priv() then calls blk_mq_quiesce_queue_nowait() and
blk_mq_unfreeze_queue(). A new request can enter the queue. The old
dispatcher can run again, use its old flag check, get the new request,
and call virtio_queue_rq(). At the same time, virtblk_freeze_priv() can
reset the device, delete the virtqueues, and free vblk->vqs. The old
dispatcher can then use a deleted virtqueue or a NULL vblk->vqs, and the
kernel can crash.

Fix this by using blk_mq_quiesce_queue(), which waits for dispatch code
that was already running. Keep the existing freeze and unfreeze order.
The queue remains quiesced until virtblk_restore_priv() calls
blk_mq_unquiesce_queue().

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: blk-mq: fix out-of-bounds read in blk_mq_free_rqs A KASAN slab-out-of-bounds read can occur in…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

blk-mq: fix out-of-bounds read in blk_mq_free_rqs

A KASAN slab-out-of-bounds read can occur in blk_mq_free_rqs() when there
is a mismatch between the number of hardware queues allocated for the IO
scheduler (et->nr_hw_queues) and the number of hardware queues in the block
tag set (set->nr_hw_queues).

This mismatch can happen if blk_mq_update_nr_hw_queues() fails halfway
through (e.g., due to memory pressure during
blk_mq_prealloc_tag_set_tags()). In this error path, the elevator is
restored with a larger number of hardware queues than the block tag set
actually has.

When the elevator is later freed, blk_mq_free_sched_tags() iterates up to
the new et->nr_hw_queues and calls blk_mq_free_rqs(). In blk_mq_free_rqs(),
it attempts to access set->tags[hctx_idx] to get the driver tags. Because
set->nr_hw_queues was not updated due to the earlier failure, set->tags
still has the old (smaller) size, leading to an out-of-bounds read.

BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in blk_mq_free_rqs+0xde/0x680
Read of size 8 at addr ffff88818d67fc28 by task syz-executor117/5839
Call Trace:
 blk_mq_free_rqs+0xde/0x680
 blk_mq_free_map_and_rqs+0x40/0xf0
 blk_mq_free_sched_tags
 blk_mq_free_sched_res+0xeb/0x280
 elevator_change_done+0x1d2/0x5c0
 elevator_change+0x34f/0x480
 elv_iosched_store+0x504/0x630
 queue_attr_store+0x207/0x2b0

To fix this, explicitly check if hctx_idx < set->nr_hw_queues before
accessing set->tags[hctx_idx]. If hctx_idx >= set->nr_hw_queues, the
hardware queue doesn't exist in the tag set, meaning there are no driver
tags to clear mappings from. In this case, safely set drv_tags to NULL. The
subsequent call to blk_mq_clear_rq_mapping() already handles a NULL
drv_tags pointer and will safely return.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: mark the inode preallocated for pNFS write layouts past EOF xfs_fs_map_blocks() marks the inode…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: mark the inode preallocated for pNFS write layouts past EOF

xfs_fs_map_blocks() marks the inode XFS_DIFLAG_PREALLOC only when it
allocates blocks for a write layout. A write layout past EOF can also
hand out allocated blocks, such as speculative preallocation. blockgc
then frees them under the layout, and another file may get them.

Mark the inode whenever a write mapping ends past EOF.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: refuse a pNFS LAYOUTCOMMIT of a range without blocks A client can commit a hole in a LAYOUTCOMMIT…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: refuse a pNFS LAYOUTCOMMIT of a range without blocks

A client can commit a hole in a LAYOUTCOMMIT, because nfsd does not
check the extents against its layouts. xfs_iomap_write_unwritten() then
allocates written blocks there. A large hole overruns the block
reservation and shuts XFS down. A small one exposes stale data.

Refuse such a range with -EIO, using XFS_BMAPI_CONVERT_ONLY.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one extent xfs_iomap_write_direct() reserves blocks…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one extent

xfs_iomap_write_direct() reserves blocks for the whole count in an
unsigned int. For a pNFS layout the client chooses that count, and an
RW LAYOUTGET for 16 TiB wraps the reservation and shuts XFS down.

xfs_bmapi_write() maps at most XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN blocks here, so cap
the count at that. nfsd asks again for the rest. The other callers get
the same mapping as before.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: clamp the pNFS layout range to the maximum file size xfs_fs_map_blocks() lets two bad layout ranges…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: clamp the pNFS layout range to the maximum file size

xfs_fs_map_blocks() lets two bad layout ranges through. An offset of
2^63 or more is negative and passes "offset > limit". A length above
the limit, such as NFS4_UINT64_MAX, wraps "offset > limit - length"
and stays unclamped. With NFS4_UINT64_MAX, a read layout is built from
an uninitialized mapping.

Reject a negative offset and one at the limit, and clamp the length.
This needs "xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one
extent".

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: restore refcount ordering for lockless socket access Before commit fb041bb7c0a9 ("locking/refcount…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: restore refcount ordering for lockless socket access

Before commit fb041bb7c0a9 ("locking/refcount: Consolidate implementations
of refcount_t"), default builds implemented refcount_inc_not_zero() using
atomic_add_unless(), which provided full memory ordering on success. The
commit removed that ordering on weakly ordered architectures, allowing
accesses after a successful reference acquisition to be reordered before
it.

Use refcount_inc_not_zero_acquire() in the IPv4 and IPv6 established
lookups and in inet_twsk_purge(), where the socket is validated again
after taking a reference.

bpf_sk_assign() can receive a socket pointer obtained through BTF
without a reference. Use acquire ordering when it takes its own reference
for a refcounted socket.

Use refcount_set_release() when setting refcounts in the SYN cookie,
TCP Fast Open, request migration, and TIME_WAIT paths. Keep the existing
TIME_WAIT smp_wmb(), which separately orders the refcount store before
ehash publication.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nvmet: reject keep-alive timeouts that would overflow nvmet_set_feat_kato() and nvmet_alloc_ctrl() convert the…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvmet: reject keep-alive timeouts that would overflow

nvmet_set_feat_kato() and nvmet_alloc_ctrl() convert the 32-bit
millisecond KATO from the host to seconds with DIV_ROUND_UP(kato, 1000).
The addition in DIV_ROUND_UP() is done in 32 bits, so any KATO above
4294966296 ms wraps around and rounds to 0 seconds. A Set Features
command with KATO 0xffffffff then succeeds but disables the keep-alive
timer: Get Features returns 0 and Keep Alive fails with Keep Alive
Timeout Invalid. A Connect command with such a KATO creates a controller
without a keep-alive timer.

The converted value has more consumers that can overflow. Get Features
multiplies it by 1000, and the timer paths multiply it by HZ in 32 bits
and arm a delay that must not exceed MAX_JIFFY_OFFSET.

Reject a KATO whose rounded value does not fit all of these. Return Keep
Alive Timeout Invalid from both Set Features and Connect. Validate Set
Features before stopping the current timer so a failed update leaves its
timeout unchanged. Round in 64 bits. A KATO of 0 keeps its current
meaning.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: dev: can_dropped_invalid_skb: drop CAN XL frames on non-CAN XL devices Sending a PF_PACKET bypasses the…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

can: dev: can_dropped_invalid_skb: drop CAN XL frames on non-CAN XL devices

Sending a PF_PACKET bypasses the CAN framework logic and can directly
reach a CAN driver's xmit() function. The PF_PACKET framework only
checks that skb->len does not exceed the net_device MTU.

For a CAN device that is not CAN XL capable, anything above CANFD_MTU
(72 bytes) is therefore dropped before it reaches the driver. However,
CAN XL frames are variable length. can_is_canxl_skb() accepts lengths in
the range CANXL_HDR_SIZE + CANXL_MIN_DLEN up to CANXL_MTU, i.e. 13 to
2060 bytes.

As a result, an ETH_P_CANXL skb with a length between 13 and 72 bytes
can pass both the MTU and the can_dropped_invalid_skb() checks.

A driver that does not support CAN XL will interpret canxl_frame->flags
as a length because of the overlap with can_frame->len. And because
CANXL_XLF is set, the resulting length is between 128 and 255. For
drivers that do not check can_frame->len before copying can_frame->data,
as most drivers do, this results in a buffer overflow of up to 247
bytes.

Drop ETH_P_CANXL skbs if the device does not have the CAN_CAP_XL
capability. Keep can_is_canxl_skb() for the validation of CAN XL skbs.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: replace ARPHRD_CAN type checks with can_get_ml_priv() Commit 4e096a18867a ("net: introduce CAN specific…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

can: replace ARPHRD_CAN type checks with can_get_ml_priv()

Commit 4e096a18867a ("net: introduce CAN specific pointer in the struct
net_device") introduced an explicit way to assign the midlayer private
pointer (dev->ml_priv) to named users like ML_PRIV_CAN. A valid pointer
returned by can_get_ml_priv() therefore identifies a real CAN device.

The referenced commit only converted the j1939 and proc code to this
check, while the other parts of the CAN subsystem still rely on
dev->type == ARPHRD_CAN.

The TUNSETLINK ioctl allows a down TUN/TAP device to set its hardware
type to ARPHRD_CAN while dev->ml_priv remains NULL. Such a repurposed
netdevice passes the ARPHRD_CAN checks.

Commit 8aa59e355949 ("can: af_can: fix NULL pointer dereference in
can_rx_register()") already made can_rx_register() reject such devices.
But can_rx_unregister() still only checks dev->type and dereferences
the NULL ml_priv when it walks the receive lists of the device.

CAN_ISOTP reaches this path: isotp_bind() ignores the return values of
can_rx_register() and binds the socket anyway. When the socket is
released or the device is unregistered, isotp_release() and
isotp_notify() remove the filters that have never been registered and
trigger the NULL pointer dereference in can_rx_unregister(). This only
requires owning a TUN/TAP device or CAP_NET_ADMIN in an unprivileged
user namespace.

Convert the remaining ARPHRD_CAN checks in af_can, bcm, gw, isotp and
raw to can_get_ml_priv().

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: protect the receive lists with a per-device lock The receive lists of a CAN device are located in the…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

can: protect the receive lists with a per-device lock

The receive lists of a CAN device are located in the device's
can_ml_priv and travel with the device when it is moved to another
network namespace. But they are protected by the per-netns
rcvlists_lock. So can_rx_unregister() needs dev_net(dev) to pick the
right lock and silently returns when the passed namespace does not
match dev_net(dev) anymore.

isotp_release() and bcm_release() leave their notifier list before they
take any lock that serializes against the netdev notifier, which runs
under RTNL. When the bound device is moved to another namespace in this
window, the notifier skips the socket and the release path has to remove
the filters itself. isotp_release() passes the socket's namespace, which
does not match dev_net(dev) anymore. bcm_rx_unreg() passes dev_net(dev),
which can_rx_unregister() reads again for its check, so a namespace
change between both reads makes the check fail as well. In both cases
can_rx_unregister() silently returns. As can_rx_register() stores
rcv->sk without a reference, the remaining receivers point to the freed
socket (isotp) or the freed op (bcm):

  BUG: KASAN: use-after-free in isotp_rcv+0x1570/0x24d0
  Read of size 1 at addr ffff888118130552 by task isotp_ns_uaf/578
   can_rcv_filter+0x4af/0x8c0
   can_receive+0x28d/0x3c0
   can_rcv+0x2a9/0x310
   __netif_receive_skb_one_core+0x21a/0x260
   process_backlog+0x210/0x760

Besides this, the lists of a device are protected by the rcvlists_lock
of the namespace that is passed in. Callers which pass dev_net(dev) read
it at different times, so the same lists may be modified under the locks
of different namespaces while the device is moved.

Taking RTNL in these release paths is no option: raw_bind(),
raw_setsockopt() and raw_release() already hold RTNL while adding and
removing up to CAN_RAW_FILTER_MAX filters per socket, which unprivileged
users can trigger repeatedly and which makes RTNL a global bottleneck.

Instead fix the root cause and add a spinlock to struct
can_dev_rcv_lists, which protects the receive lists of a CAN device or
the 'any' CAN device lists of a namespace. It is initialized in
can_set_ml_priv(), which is used by all CAN network devices. With this,
can_rx_unregister() finds the subscription independently of the
current namespace of the device. The protocols keep the device valid
with their tracked references. The per-netns rcvlists_lock only protects
the receive list statistics anymore, and CAN_RAW, CAN_BCM and CAN_ISOTP
pass the namespace that has been used for can_rx_register().

So isotp_release() and bcm_release() now remove their filters correctly
without RTNL, and raw_release(), raw_setsockopt(), raw_bind() and
isotp_bind() do not need RTNL anymore and add and remove their filters
under lock_sock(). To serialize bind() with NETDEV_UNREGISTER, bind()
publishes the device inside the RCU section of its lookup, and
raw_notify() and isotp_notify() recheck the bound device under lock_sock().
As RTNL does not keep NETDEV_DOWN out of bind() anymore, bind() checks
IFF_UP after publishing the bound device, with a barrier pair against
raw_notify() and isotp_notify(), so a down transition during bind() is
still reported with ENETDOWN.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: raw, isotp: copy socket options outside of lock_sock() The CAN_RAW and CAN_ISOTP specific socket options…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

can: raw, isotp: copy socket options outside of lock_sock()

The CAN_RAW and CAN_ISOTP specific socket options are copied from and
to user space while holding lock_sock(). A copy that faults or stalls,
e.g. on a userfaultfd or FUSE backed mapping, holds lock_sock() for its
whole duration.

raw_notify() and isotp_notify() take lock_sock() of a socket that is
bound to the vanishing device while holding RTNL. As the CAN_RAW
options can also be changed on a bound socket, a stalled copy can block
RTNL on an unregistration or namespace change of the bound device.
Before "can: protect the receive lists with a per-device lock",
raw_setsockopt() even held RTNL itself during the copy. CAN_ISOTP only
copies its options for unbound sockets, which isotp_notify() skips
without taking lock_sock().

Keep the user space copies out of the locked sections: Check the option
name and length and copy the option values, including the CAN_RAW_FILTER
filters, to kernel memory before lock_sock(). raw_setsockopt_locked()
and isotp_setsockopt_locked() get the copied values directly and drop
their now redundant length checks and copies. As a side effect, a
failing copy can not leave partially overwritten options behind
anymore. In raw_getsockopt() duplicate the filters under lock_sock() and
copy them to user space after release_sock().

As the option name and length are now checked before lock_sock(), the
order of the checks in isotp_setsockopt() and accordingly the order of
the returned error values changes. This is in line with POSIX, which
does not define an order in which multiple error conditions are
detected and reported.

The generic SOL_SOCKET options in sk_setsockopt() are not affected by
this patch.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: dev: can_fill_info(): don't wake up controller if interface is down If the interface is down, the CAN…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

can: dev: can_fill_info(): don't wake up controller if interface is down

If the interface is down, the CAN controller might be powered down and
its clocks gated. Don't call do_get_berr_counter() to read the bus error
counters if the interface is down, and adjust can_get_size() to match.

This removes one trigger for a synchronous external abort seen on
i.MX8QXP when "ip link show" is run on a flexcan interface that was
never brought up. The underlying cause is platform-specific: on i.MX8QXP
the CAN clocks are gated through the SCU LPCG and the subsystem shares
the IMX_SC_R_CAN_0 power domain, and there is a window after
pm_runtime_resume_and_get() returns where the clock has not reached the
module yet. This patch avoids the netlink query path while the interface
is down, but does not root-cause the LPCG window itself.

As a result, IFLA_CAN_BERR_COUNTER is no longer reported for down
interfaces. Userspace must treat the attribute as optional.

The issue was triggered on an i.MX8QXP board by running "ip link show"
without ever bringing the interface up:

    Internal error: synchronous external abort: 0000000096000210

    pc : flexcan_read_le+0x0/0x18
    lr : flexcan_get_berr_counter+0x4c/0x8c
    Call trace:
     flexcan_read_le+0x0/0x18
     flexcan_get_berr_counter+0x4c/0x8c
     can_fill_info+0x1f8/0x434
     rtnl_fill_ifinfo+0x8fc/0xbb4
     rtnl_dump_ifinfo+0x364/0x448

This is the same class of problem fixed for m_can in
commit 91a55c72a821 ("can: m_can: m_can_get_berr_counter(): don't
wake up controller if interface is down").

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: fix truncate racing with PMD zapping zap_huge_pmd_folio() removes the rmap before calling…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/huge_memory: fix truncate racing with PMD zapping

zap_huge_pmd_folio() removes the rmap before calling folio_mark_dirty().
If this was the last mapping, truncation can skip unmapping the folio
and proceed without waiting for the PMD lock, racing with dirtying.

ifs_set_range_dirty() can oops if MADV_DONTNEED races with
ftruncate() on XFS, when we get the folio set dirty after it was found
to not be mapped anymore.

Move folio_mark_dirty() and folio_mark_accessed() before rmap removal,
matching the PTE zap path. This keeps the folio mapped while updating
its state, so truncation must wait for the page table lock.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: simplify comment and description ]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: fix zapping migration entries for device-private THPs A PMD migration entry can refer to a…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/huge_memory: fix zapping migration entries for device-private THPs

A PMD migration entry can refer to a device-private folio.
zap_huge_pmd_folio() checks the folio type instead of the entry type,
so it treats such a migration entry as a device-private entry.

Installing the migration entry already removed the reverse mapping and
dropped the mapping reference. Zapping it must not repeat those
operations. Concurrent MADV_DONTNEED during migration back to system
memory can trigger this.

Check the PMD entry type using pmd_is_device_private_entry().

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: simplify description ]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: always recheck the pmd in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() drops the…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/khugepaged: always recheck the pmd in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp()

try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() drops the PTE lock after it has cleared the
page table, and takes the PMD lock and the PTE lock to remove it.

In between, MADV_DONTNEED with CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM can reclaim the
page table. The pmd_same() check is supposed to handle this, but it is
only done with CONFIG_SPLIT_PTE_PTLOCKS.

Fix it by performing the check unconditionally.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: adjust description ]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: fix PMD table lock leak in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() For a private mapping with…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/khugepaged: fix PMD table lock leak in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp()

For a private mapping with userfaultfd, try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp()
takes the PMD table lock before it maps the page table for the second time.
If that (pte_offset_map_rw_nolock) fails, because the page table vanished
in the meantime due to concurrent page table reclaim, it leaves through
the abort label, where the PMD table lock is unlocked if it differs from
PTE table lock.

In case the PMD table lock and the PTE table lock match, which is the
case without CONFIG_SPLIT_PTE_PTLOCKS after pte_offset_map_rw_nolock()
failed, we miss to unlock the PMD table.

To fix it, forget the PTE table lock when we unmap+unlock the PTE table.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: move the ptl = NULL handling; rewrite description, drop wrong comments ]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: preserve dirty bits when collapsing PTE-mapped THPs try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() clears PTEs…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/khugepaged: preserve dirty bits when collapsing PTE-mapped THPs

try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() clears PTEs without transferring their dirty
bits to the folio. A shmem read fault can map a clean folio writable, so
a later store only dirties the PTE. Losing that dirty bit allows reclaim
to discard modified data.

The assumption that regular files are read-only is also obsolete since
commit 1b6444331bebb ("mm/khugepaged: enable clean pagecache folio collapse
for writable files"). In any case, transferring PTE dirty bits to the folio
when removing mappings (and while the folio is still mapped) is the right
thing to do.

Use get_and_clear_ptes() to collect the dirty bits and mark the folio
dirty before unmapping it. Update the comment.

This was reproduced with shmem using MADV_COLLAPSE followed by
MADV_PAGEOUT.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: adjust comment; simplify description; cover file-thp as well ]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: recheck the PUD under PTL in follow_pud_mask() follow_pud_mask() reads the PUD without a lock.
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/gup: recheck the PUD under PTL in follow_pud_mask()

follow_pud_mask() reads the PUD without a lock. If it is a leaf, it takes
the lock and calls follow_huge_pud(), which reads the entry again, but
only tests whether it is present.

A leaf can be zapped concurrently and a page fault can fill the empty
entry with a page table.

This currently only applies when device-dax makes use of PUD entries,
and the fault after e.g., MADV_DONTNEED would find THPs to be disabled.

That requires a sequence like

1) Fault in the PUD
2) Disable THP
3) Have GUP race against concurrent MADV_DONTNEED + refault

Which is rather unlikely to happen in practice, which is why we never
received a report about such a problem.

Before commit 1b1676180246 ("mm/gup: handle huge pud for
follow_pud_mask()"), we performed that check in follow_devmap_pud() by
testing for pud_devmap().

Let's fix it by just structuring follow_pud_mask() similar to
follow_pmd_mask(), minus protnone stuff that does not apply and minus
FOLL_SPLIT_PMD handling. That makes it much easier to spot any such
inconsistencies.

Perform the pud_bad() check early in follow_pmd_mask() and just forward
the PUD value. We can drop the pud_present() check in follow_huge_pud(),
just like we have in follow_huge_pmd().

Even though we are performing more changes than strictly necessary, the
fix should be easy to backport.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: fix clearing folios in memfd_pin_folios() memfd_pin_folios() pins folios obtained directly from the…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/gup: fix clearing folios in memfd_pin_folios()

memfd_pin_folios() pins folios obtained directly from the page cache
without checking whether they are uptodate. However, shmem fallocate()
can leave newly allocated folios uncleared and not uptodate. Callers
such as udmabuf can then expose uninitialized memory to userspace.

Clear non-uptodate folios and mark them uptodate under the folio lock
before returning them to the caller.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: simplify description and comment ]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: fix out-of-bounds write for nr_pages == 0 in GUP-fast With nr_pages == 0, GUP-fast still enters its…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/gup: fix out-of-bounds write for nr_pages == 0 in GUP-fast

With nr_pages == 0, GUP-fast still enters its page table walk and can
write past the caller's page array. The old end <= start check caught
empty ranges, but was replaced with an overflow check.

Users such as OrangeFS can pass a zero page count derived from a
userspace-supplied length. So let's return zero for nr_pages == 0 before
starting the walk, just like GUP-slow.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: simplify description ]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: check for overflow when converting nr_pages to bytes in GUP-fast The overflow check in…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/gup: check for overflow when converting nr_pages to bytes in GUP-fast

The overflow check in gup_fast_fallback() only covers the addition to
start. The preceding nr_pages << PAGE_SHIFT can already have truncated
the length on 32bit.

Users such as RapidIO's rio_dma_transfer() can derive such page counts
from a 64-bit userspace length.

Let's just check_shl_overflow() to reject any such overflow with
-EOVERFLOW early.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/userfaultfd: write-lock the VMA before waking waiters when unregistering userfaultfd_unregister() wakes…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/userfaultfd: write-lock the VMA before waking waiters when unregistering

userfaultfd_unregister() wakes pending missing faults before clearing the
VMA's userfaultfd registration. With per-VMA fault locking, holding
mmap_lock for write does not prevent another fault from queuing after
the wakeup but before userfaultfd_clear_vma() write-locks the VMA. That
waiter can then remain asleep indefinitely.

Call vma_start_write() before waking waiters. Existing fault handlers
queue themselves before dropping the VMA read lock, and new readers are
excluded until mmap_write_unlock().

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_gather: fix flushing ranges with 4 GiB or larger __tlb_adjust_range() takes the size of the range which…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mmu_gather: fix flushing ranges with 4 GiB or larger

__tlb_adjust_range() takes the size of the range which has to be flushed
as an unsigned int. Its callers, tlb_flush_{pte,pmd,pud,p4d}_range(), get
and pass an unsigned long. Consequently, a range that is 4 GiB or larger
gets truncated, possibly to 0.

On arm64 with hugetlb, a 64k kernel can have 16 GiB hugetlb folios
mapped contiguously at the PMD level and flush them when unmapping, and a
16k kernel can flush 64 GiB PUDs through tlb_unshare_pmd_ptdesc(). So
at least these two scenarios are affected.

Fix it by flushing the proper range instead of the truncated one by
properly using "unsigned long" for range_size.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: use two-tab indent, simplify description ]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_notifier: finish non-blocking interval invalidation on error When an ordinary MMU notifier rejects a…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mmu_notifier: finish non-blocking interval invalidation on error

When an ordinary MMU notifier rejects a non-blocking invalidation, the
interval invalidation started beforehand is left unfinished: the caller
skips mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_end(). Subsequent interval notifier
operations can then wait forever.

The only in-tree trigger is nouveau SVM, which uses both notifier types
and rejects non-blocking invalidations. Reaping via the OOM reaper or
process_mrelease() can therefore leave the GPU fault worker stuck,
holding a reference that prevents the dying process's address space
and memory from being freed.

End the interval invalidation when an ordinary notifier fails a
non-blocking invalidation, like mn_itree_invalidate() already does when
an interval notifier fails. Make that handling clearer in the
documentation of mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_start_nonblock().

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: simplify description, update function doc ]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_notifier: set ->mm only after mmgrab() Radeon uses a non-NULL notifier->mm to decide whether to call…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mmu_notifier: set ->mm only after mmgrab()

Radeon uses a non-NULL notifier->mm to decide whether to call
mmu_interval_notifier_remove() when freeing a buffer object.
__mmu_interval_notifier_insert() sets ->mm before validating the range,
so a wrapping userptr range can leave ->mm set after insertion fails.
Cleanup then tries to remove an unregistered notifier for which no mm
reference was acquired.

Set ->mm only after mmgrab(), once insertion can no longer fail. While
we could fix radeon's code instead, setting ->mm on success only makes
the code more robust.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: simplify description ]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/madvise: fix data loss from MADV_FREE on a KSM page MADV_FREE can clear the dirty flag of a singly mapped…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/madvise: fix data loss from MADV_FREE on a KSM page

MADV_FREE can clear the dirty flag of a singly mapped KSM folio. The
folio remains in the stable tree and can gain new mappings without being
dirtied again. Once marked lazyfree, reclaim can discard data that those
mappings still need.

KSM always marks a folio dirty when converting it to a KSM folio in
try_to_merge_one_page(). Marking a folio lazyfree clears PG_swapbacked
but leaves PG_dirty unchanged. Preserving PG_dirty makes reclaim restore
PG_swapbacked instead of discarding the folio. This also protects folios
that were already lazyfree when KSM converted them.

Skip KSM folios before clearing their dirty flag, checking under the
folio lock to serialize with KSM conversion.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/memory: reject remote COW faults on PFN mappings When handling a COW fault without a normal source page…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/memory: reject remote COW faults on PFN mappings

When handling a COW fault without a normal source page (PFN mappings),
__wp_page_copy_user() copies from the faulting user address. For remote
faults, this accesses the wrong address space, resulting in wrong data
getting copied.

For example, user_events updates an enable bit in the registering
process's memory. If that memory needs to be faulted in,
user_event_enabler_fault_fixup() calls fixup_user_fault() from a work
item. Placing the enable bit in a private PFN mapping can trigger this
remote COW path.

Reject these faults with VM_FAULT_SIGBUS when the target mm differs from
current->mm: remote faults. Ordinary (non-PFN) mappings are not affected.

The user-address copy dates back to commit 6aab341e0a28 ("mm: re-architect
the VM_UNPAGED logic"); likely, actual ways to get remote faults in
there on COW PFN mappings appeared afterwards. But the fix is simple and
straight forward.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: simplify comment and description ]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix unmap_mapping_range() beyond 4 GiB on 32-bit Commit 9eab0421fa94 ("mm: fix unmap_mapping_range high…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm: fix unmap_mapping_range() beyond 4 GiB on 32-bit

Commit 9eab0421fa94 ("mm: fix unmap_mapping_range high bits shift bug")
made holebegin and holelen unsigned before they are shifted, by casting
them to pgoff_t. That is an unsigned long: on a 32-bit kernel the cast
cuts off the upper half of the two loff_t values, so a hole which begins
at 4 GiB or beyond is taken for one in the first 4 GiB of the file.

truncate_pagecache() passes the new size of the file and asks for private
COWed pages to be unmapped as well. If a file of 6 GiB is truncated to
5 GiB, everything from 1 GiB on is unmapped, and what a process has
written to a private mapping of the range between 1 GiB and 5 GiB is
lost: it reads the contents of the file again.

Where the range has an end, the wrong range is unmapped instead of the
right one. The page cache copes with that, as it unmaps every folio that
it removes. The callers which only have unmap_mapping_range() to get
rid of user mappings do not, for example drm_vma_node_unmap(), whose fake
offsets reach beyond 4 GiB on 32-bit, and revoke_iomem() with physical
addresses of more than 32 bits.

Cast to u64 instead. Nothing changes for 64-bit kernels.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix unkillable fault loop on MAP_DROPPABLE memory handle_mm_fault() suppresses VM_FAULT_OOM for…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm: fix unkillable fault loop on MAP_DROPPABLE memory

handle_mm_fault() suppresses VM_FAULT_OOM for VM_DROPPABLE mappings.

For user-mode faults, pending signals are processed before retrying the
access. Kernel-mode faults on user buffers instead return directly to
the faulting instruction.

With persistent allocation failures (esp. memcg limits), a syscall,
such as write(), can therefore loop while not dropping locks.

Only suppress VM_FAULT_OOM when FAULT_FLAG_USER is set, allowing
kernel-mode faults and GUP to fail and signal allocation errors.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: simplify description ]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix deadlock of mremap() against UFFDIO_MOVE With per-VMA locks, UFFDIO_MOVE can run concurrently with…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm: fix deadlock of mremap() against UFFDIO_MOVE

With per-VMA locks, UFFDIO_MOVE can run concurrently with mremap()
on different VMAs in the same mm. Those VMAs can share page tables, so
both operations can acquire the same pair of page-table locks.

UFFDIO_MOVE orders the locks by address, while mremap() takes the source
lock first. These conflicting orders can deadlock; mremap() holding
mmap_lock for writing no longer helps.

Move double_pt_lock() and double_pt_unlock() to mm/internal.h and use
them for all page-table moves in mremap(). Preserve the source entry
checks after acquiring both locks. Remove the comments claiming that
exclusive mmap_lock makes lock ordering irrelevant.

In move_ptes(), make sure to just recheck source and destination PMD
after taking the locks and drop the overly-long comment.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: use new helpers consistently; simplify description and comments;
         move_ptes() fixup ]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: reset the unstable trees of all nodes Each full scan resets ksm_nr_node_ids unstable tree roots.
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/ksm: reset the unstable trees of all nodes

Each full scan resets ksm_nr_node_ids unstable tree roots. Enabling
merge_across_nodes resets this count to 1, even if per-node roots were
previously allocated.

So when toggling "merge_across_nodes" 0 -> 1 -> 0, a scan that starts
while the setting is 1 and continues after switching back to 0 can
encounter stale unstable tree roots, resulting in UAF.

Only root is allowed to change "merge_across_nodes", and the documented
sequence is: "merge_across_nodes setting can be changed only when there
are no ksm shared pages in the system: set run 2 to unmerge pages first,
then to 1 after changing merge_across_nodes, to remerge according to the
new setting."

Let's fix it by tracking in ksm_nr_node_ids the actual number of
allocated tree roots.

remove_all_stable_nodes() and ksm_check_stable_tree() will now scan
more tree roots (skipping the empty ones), which is harmless.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: fix use of a freed anon_vma at swap-in A folio read from a swap slot previously shared by KSM can…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/ksm: fix use of a freed anon_vma at swap-in

A folio read from a swap slot previously shared by KSM can remain in the
swap cache after the process that first mapped it exits. Its anon_vma
can then be freed, so ksm_might_need_to_copy() must not dereference it
to compare roots.

Doing so can result in some false-positives, resulting in the reverse
mapping missing the new folio mapping, preventing migration and reclaim.

SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU allows individual anon_vma objects to be reused
immediately after freeing. A stale pointer can then refer to another
anon_vma whose root matches, even though the target VMA is not linked
to that anon_vma.

Move the anonymous rmap compatibility checks into
folio_anon_rmap_compatible(). Keep the page-index check and compare the
folio's anon_vma pointer against the VMA's own anon_vma and root first.

If neither matches, bite the bullet and walk the VMA's anon_vma_chain.
The VMA keeps these anon_vmas alive, and finding a match guarantees that
reverse mapping can find the new mapping.

Lorenzo Stoakes says in a private discussion:

  "This isn't quite equivalent to the existing check.

  Every anon_vma in an anon_vma_chain shares the same root, but if you
  split a VMA then fork both of them like this:

                  VMA A
               /        \         <split>
            VMA B      VMA C
               \        /
        root <- anon_vma 1
               ----^ ^----        <fork>
              /   parent  \
        anon_vma 2   anon_vma 3
             |            |
           VMA D        VMA E

  VMA's D and E both get their own new
  anon_vma's such that:

  VMA D: anon_vma 2 -> anon_vma 1 -> root
  VMA E: anon_vma 3 -> anon_vma 1 -> root

  And if you found a folio referencing anon_vma 2, the existing check:

	anon_vma->root == vma->anon-vma->root

  Would be true for VMA's B, C, D & E.

  However after your change it'd be true for VMA D only, as it's the only
  one with anon_vma 2 in its anon_vma_chain.

  Whether or not that could actually happen in practice... 🙂 I don't
  know.

  [...] after your change it'd be true for VMA D only, as it's the only
  one with anon_vma 2 in its anon_vma_chain. [...] I would [...] say that
  you are making the test stricter but more correct.
"

If this affects performance when KSM was never even involved, we could
just track whether KSM ever merged anything and just skip these checks.

There isn't really a lot we can do otherwise: for mapped folios we might
be able to use folio_get_anon_vma(), but for unmapped folios there really
is no easy way to see if the anon_vma is still valid.

Document the (confusing) lifetime requirements of folio_anon_vma().

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: check large swap-cache folios before mapping them KSM folios are always small, but their shared swap…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/ksm: check large swap-cache folios before mapping them

KSM folios are always small, but their shared swap slots can be read
back as part of a large folio in the swap cache. ksm_might_need_to_copy()
skips large folios, so another process can map a page with an incompatible
anon_vma or page index. Reverse mapping then cannot find the new
mapping, preventing migration or reclaim.

Apply the same compatibility checks to large folios as to small ones.
Pass the page corresponding to the swap entry and copy only that page
when necessary. In do_swap_page()'s copy path, decrement only that slot's
swap count, because the source swap-cache folio can now be large.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/vma: call ->may_split() before a partial merge A driver can use the ->may_split() hook to forbid a VMA…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/vma: call ->may_split() before a partial merge

A driver can use the ->may_split() hook to forbid a VMA boundary at
certain addresses.

A device-dax device is a character device that gives raw access to a
range of memory through mmap(). device-dax refuses any address that is not
a multiple of the device's alignment through vm_ops->may_split.

vma_merge_existing_range() can move boundaries, but does not call
vm_ops->may_split.

If a range at the edge of a VMA gets the attributes of the adjacent VMA,
the function moves only that range over to the neighbour: one VMA shrinks
and the other grows. This is a partial merge, and vma_modify() tries it
before any split.

Take a device-dax VMA that lies next to another VMA of the same file.
The user calls mprotect() on the one page of the first VMA that touches
the second VMA, and asks for the protection that the second VMA already
has. The result is a partial merge. It puts the boundary inside a 1 GiB
mapping, which is a single leaf entry at the PUD level.

As part of the merge, the kernel looks for a huge PMD to split at the
new boundary. That code does not expect a PUD leaf:

    vma_merge_existing_range()
      commit_merge()
        vma_adjust_trans_huge()
          split_huge_pmd_address()
            mm_find_pmd()
              treats the PUD leaf as a pointer to a PMD table,
              so the "table" is the device memory that the leaf maps
            __split_huge_pmd()
              reads a PMD that the user wrote to the device memory
              folio_put() on the folio that this PMD names

Bad. While the code must at some point be taught to split PUD entries as
well, the issue here is that we move VMA boundaries such that they are
incompatible with the driver.

Fix this by calling ->may_split() on the address that a partial merge
would move the boundary to, and by abandoning the merge if the driver
refuses. vma_modify() then tries the split, which fails with -EINVAL.

Factor out existing split handling into check_split() and reuse it.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: improve description; cleanup the code ]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: split huge PUDs when adjusting VMA boundaries PFN mappings such as VFIO PCI BAR mappings can…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/huge_memory: split huge PUDs when adjusting VMA boundaries

PFN mappings such as VFIO PCI BAR mappings can use PUD leaves while
allowing VMA splits at page granularity. However, vma_adjust_trans_huge()
only handles PMDs.

After faulting a writable PUD-sized VFIO BAR mapping, changing its first
page to read-only with mprotect() makes the PMD walk treat the PUD leaf
as a PMD table. Applying MADV_DONTFORK to the first PMD-sized chunk leaves
the PUD spanning two VMAs: the PMD-aligned boundary skips splitting.

Walk the page tables once at each adjusted boundary and split a huge
PUD or PMD leaf as needed. Handle PUD leaves even when the boundary is
PMD-aligned.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/vma: don't leak the charge for stack growth acct_stack_growth() charges stack expansion even without…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/vma: don't leak the charge for stack growth

acct_stack_growth() charges stack expansion even without VM_ACCOUNT.
This can happen for read-only or MAP_NORESERVE mappings created with
MAP_GROWSDOWN. Unmapping these VMAs does not release the charge, leaking
Committed_AS.

Only check and charge growth for VM_ACCOUNT VMAs, matching mremap().
Unaccounted growth skips the overcommit check while remaining subject
to the other stack-growth limits.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/cma: don't release CMA pages still in use When a driver calls dma_free_contiguous() before quiescing DMA…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/cma: don't release CMA pages still in use

When a driver calls dma_free_contiguous() before quiescing DMA, the
page might still have a reference from the device.
put_page_testzero() there returns false, WARN fires, but the code proceeds
to free_contig_frozen_range() putting a live page onto buddy and clearing
the bitmap. A subsequent allocation can hand the same PFN to a new
owner while the original holder still references it.

A concurrent put_page() that drops the last reference between the
testzero loop and free_contig_frozen_range() can double-queue the page
via page->lru, corrupting buddy lists.

Avoid the corruption by not freeing a CMA region if any of the
pages inside are still in use.

Make it explicit in the warning that the driver allowed a leak.

While at it, use page_ref_freeze() to make the semantics clearer and
switch to pr_warn_ratelimited().

[ david: use page_ref_freeze() + pr_warn_ratelimited() ]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/memory-tiers: unregister empty tiers outside memory_tier_lock When offlining a node's last memory empties…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/memory-tiers: unregister empty tiers outside memory_tier_lock

When offlining a node's last memory empties its tier,
clear_node_memory_tier() calls device_unregister() while holding
memory_tier_lock. A concurrent sysfs read can hold a kernfs active
reference and block in nodelist_show() on that mutex. device_unregister()
then waits in kernfs_drain() for the read to finish and release its active
reference, while the reader waits for the offlining task to release the
mutex.

Return the node's former tier from clear_node_memory_tier(), making the
helper more similar to set_node_memory_tier(), which also returns a
memory_tier pointer. Let the caller unlink an empty tier under
memory_tier_lock before rebuilding demotion targets, then unregister its
device after dropping the lock.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: khugepaged: fix readahead lock inversion in collapse_file() collapse_file() can call…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

khugepaged: fix readahead lock inversion in collapse_file()

collapse_file() can call page_cache_sync_readahead() while still holding
source folios locked. If truncate holds mapping->invalidate_lock
exclusively and waits for one of those folios, readahead waits for
invalidate_lock and neither side can make progress.

We need to release those folio locks before starting readahead. On a page
cache miss, roll back first, populate the collapse range, and retry once.
Doing readahead after rollback avoids an extra pass when all folios are
already present. If another miss occurs on retry, give up rather than keep
retrying while truncate or reclaim removes folios.

Keep page_cache_sync_readahead() and wait for read I/O with
filemap_lock_folio(), releasing each folio before moving to the next. The
existing uptodate check during collapse still handles read errors.

Shmem uses shmem_get_folio() for swapin and fallocated folios without
taking mapping->invalidate_lock, so it is unaffected.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: check folio->mapping under folio lock in memfd_pin_folios() memfd_pin_folios() pins folios from the…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/gup: check folio->mapping under folio lock in memfd_pin_folios()

memfd_pin_folios() pins folios from the page cache without taking the
folio lock. khugepaged or MADV_COLLAPSE can therefore replace a folio
after checking its refcount while memfd_pin_folios() still pins the old
folio. The caller then receives a folio which is no longer part of the
memfd.

For udmabuf and iommufd, this can cause data corruption: DMA accesses
the detached folio rather than the live memfd contents. DMA reads can
return stale data, while DMA writes update the detached copy and are
lost from the live memfd. The detached folio remains pinned, so these
accesses do not constitute a use-after-free or target another
application's memory. For memfd live update, the stale contents can
reappear in the memfd after handover.

Lock the folio and recheck folio->mapping before pinning it, like other
page cache users do. If the folio was removed, retry the folio lookup
from the index that was removed.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: fail the mount if the casefold flag has changed An unprivileged user in a user namespace can repeatedly…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: fail the mount if the casefold flag has changed

An unprivileged user in a user namespace can repeatedly trigger a kernel
warning with their own overlay mounts. They do so by changing the
casefold flag of the topmost layer's empty root, the top directory of
that layer, after the layers are set and before the mount is created.

The casefold flag of a directory makes name lookups in that directory
case-insensitive. All layers of an overlay must agree on casefolding.

ovl_mount_dir_check() reads the casefold flag of a layer root when
fsconfig() sets that layer, and saves the result in ofs->casefold. The
mount is created later, by another fsconfig() call with
FSCONFIG_CMD_CREATE.

The casefold flag of an empty directory can be changed.

The casefold flag of the overlay root must match ofs->casefold.
ovl_get_root() copies the flag from the topmost layer root, as it is
when the mount is created. On a mismatch, ovl_get_root() only does a
WARN_ON(), and the mount continues. The check is not a WARN_ON_ONCE(),
so each such mount warns again.

An unprivileged user needs CONFIG_UNICODE, and a tmpfs mounted with the
casefold option in their namespace.

Reproduced by changing the casefold flag of the empty upper directory
after the layers were set and before FSCONFIG_CMD_CREATE, with tmpfs and
ext4 layers, and as uid 1000 in a user namespace.

Fix this by replacing the WARN_ON() with a check that fails the mount
with -EINVAL.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: do not let chattr change the casefold flag chattr +F or -F on an overlay directory can make the…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: do not let chattr change the casefold flag

chattr +F or -F on an overlay directory can make the directory, or the
whole mount, unusable. Lookups of the directory, and lookups in it, then
fail. From code inspection, the caller only needs to own the directory.
The upper filesystem must support casefolding: ext4 or f2fs with the
casefold feature, or tmpfs with the casefold option.

chattr +F and -F set and clear FS_CASEFOLD_FL, the casefold flag of a
directory. The flag enables casefolding (case-insensitive name lookup)
for the directory. All directories of an overlay must match the casefold
state that was recorded at mount time, and ovl_lookup_single() enforces
this:

- A lookup in a directory that does not match fails with -ESTALE.
- A lookup of the directory itself fails with -EREMOTE.

ovl_fileattr_set() copies the directory up, which creates it in the
upper layer if it only existed in a lower layer. It then passes
FS_CASEFOLD_FL on to the upper filesystem. The upper filesystem accepts
the change if the upper directory is empty, regardless of what the
merged directory contains. The merged directory is the one that the user
sees, with the names from the upper and the lower directories.

After the change the upper directory no longer matches the mount. If the
directory is the root of the overlay, the whole mount is affected.

The flag can also change without chattr +F or -F. chattr reads all flags
of a directory, changes one and writes all of them back. For a directory
that only exists in a lower layer, overlayfs reads the flags from the
lower filesystem. xfs with the ascii-ci feature reports FS_CASEFOLD_FL
on every inode, but never sets S_CASEFOLD, the inode flag that overlayfs
compares with the mount. So its directories count as not casefolded.
With a lower layer on such an xfs and an upper layer on ext4 with the
casefold feature, chattr +A on a lower-only directory therefore sets
FS_CASEFOLD_FL on the new, empty upper directory.

Reproduced as root on tmpfs and on ext4 with chattr +F or -F on an
overlay directory whose upper directory was empty. Afterwards lookups
below it failed with ESTALE, and lookups of the directory itself failed
with EREMOTE. The chattr +A case was seen once, on a kernel with an
earlier form of this patch that still passed the caller's flag on:
lookups of the directory failed with EREMOTE.

Fix this by returning -EOPNOTSUPP if FS_IOC_SETFLAGS, the only call that
can change the flag, asks for a casefold flag on a directory that does
not agree with the casefold state of the mount. This also refuses the
chattr +A case above.

[amir: check the flag against the casefold state of the mount instead of
 reading back the flags]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: fix whiteout creation in casefolded directories unlink and rmdir fail with EINVAL on an overlay with…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: fix whiteout creation in casefolded directories

unlink and rmdir fail with EINVAL on an overlay with casefolded
(case-insensitive) layers, if the name exists in a lower layer.
Casefolded layers need CONFIG_UNICODE. Root can mount such an overlay,
and so can an unprivileged user in a user namespace, with tmpfs layers.

Overlayfs does not change a lower layer. To remove a name that exists
there, it hides the name with a marker file, a whiteout. It creates the
whiteout in the work directory, a scratch directory on the upper
filesystem, and renames it over the name in the upper directory:

- ovl_whiteout() creates the whiteout with mknod, or as a hard link to
  an earlier whiteout.
- ovl_cleanup_and_whiteout() then prepares the rename with
  start_renaming_two_dentries(), which returns -EINVAL if the source or
  the target dentry is unhashed, that is, not in the dentry hash table.

With casefolded directories, both dentries can be unhashed:

- The target. Lookup in a casefolded directory leaves a negative dentry
  unhashed, so the rename target is unhashed if the name does not exist
  in the upper directory.
- The source, which is the new whiteout. tmpfs hashes a dentry when
  mknod or link makes it positive, but ext4 does not, so on ext4 the
  source is unhashed as well.

The cleanup after the failure also refuses an unhashed dentry, so on
ext4 the whiteout is left behind in the work directory.

Reproduced with rm and rmdir on casefolded tmpfs and ext4 layers, also
as uid 1000 in a user namespace.

Fix this by creating the whiteout with ovl_create_temp(), which repeats
the lookup if the new dentry is unhashed. Prepare the rename with
start_renaming_dentry(), which looks up the target name with the
directories locked. The caller looked the name up without a lock, so
return -ESTALE if the name now refers to a different inode.

[amir: pass the name used for lookup instead of taking a name snapshot]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/sched: clamp skb->queue_mapping before indexing the tx queue This issue was caught by Sashiko (nipa).
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: clamp skb->queue_mapping before indexing the tx queue

This issue was caught by Sashiko (nipa). A producer-side path cap is
already merged (ea4d4b5dddb5); this patch adds the matching consumer-side
caps.

The issue:
The tx queue is picked and capped in netdev_core_pick_tx() before the
__dev_xmit_skb() qdisc enqueue path. A tc BPF program running inside an
egress qdisc (not clsact) can then change __sk_buff->queue_mapping; that
store is never re-checked. bpf_convert_ctx_access() bounds it only by
NO_QUEUE_MAPPING, not by the device's queue count.

Two consumers read the stale value:

  - On dequeue, qdisc_restart() calls netdev_get_tx_queue(), which
    indexes dev->_tx[]. netdev_get_tx_queue() guards it with just a
    DEBUG_NET_WARN_ON_ONCE, so sch_direct_xmit() takes the out-of-bounds
    txq->_xmit_lock and writes txq->xmit_lock_owner past the end of the
    allocation on non-lltx devices such as ifb. Drivers that index their
    rings from skb_get_queue_mapping() (ex: ifb) go out of range the same
    way.

  - On enqueue, taprio_enqueue() indexes q->qdiscs[] with the same value;
    the array is sized dev->num_tx_queues. A duplicating netem on a child
    qdisc clones the skb and re-enqueues the clone at the taprio root
    (qdisc_root_bh()) through a direct rootq->enqueue() call, so the value
    reaches taprio_enqueue() before any dequeue cap runs.

The Fix:
Cap the mapping at the consumers and write the capped value back, so the
qdisc's _tx[] lookup, the taprio q->qdiscs[] lookup and any later driver
read stay in range.

On the dequeue side the cap folds into the dequeue path instead of a
separate walk over the returned list: dequeue_skb() caps the head, and
each bulk helper caps the element it appends. For a qdisc that is not
TCQ_F_ONETXQUEUE, netdev_cap_txqueue() logs a ratelimited notice and
selects queue 0.

A TCQ_F_ONETXQUEUE qdisc is bound to a single tx queue: dequeue_skb() uses
q->dev_queue for the frozen check, the BQL limit and the trace point, while
qdisc_restart() transmits on the skb's queue. Capping an out-of-range
mapping to queue 0 would therefore send a per-queue child's skb through a
different queue than the one it was dequeued for. On mq, mqprio, taprio and
htb offload children, a stopped queue 0 could then park the list in
q->gso_skb, and the later wake would schedule queue 0's own child instead
of this qdisc. Pin a TCQ_F_ONETXQUEUE mapping to the qdisc's own queue to
keep the documented invariant.

The pin covers every mapping, not only an out-of-range one: an in-range
mapping that a filter sets on one of those per-queue children is rewritten
to the child's own queue, and this path does not call netdev_cap_txqueue(),
so it logs no notice. On a single-queue device qdisc_create() sets
TCQ_F_ONETXQUEUE, so the one-queue trigger described below also takes this
branch and is corrected without a notice.

That also keeps a bulk list on one queue by construction: every element of
a TCQ_F_ONETXQUEUE qdisc, including a follower changed by a filter, is
pinned to q->dev_queue before it is appended. The fast bulk helper
therefore needs no head comparison and no skb_bad_txq requeue; the slow
helper, used only by non-ONETXQUEUE qdiscs, still compares and requeues a
mismatched follower, where a wake on any queue reschedules q.

On the enqueue side taprio_enqueue() caps the mapping against
real_num_tx_queues and writes it back before selecting q->qdiscs[queue], so
a duplicating child cannot steer the clone out of the array.

Conditions to recreate the bug:
The dequeue path: load a SCHED_CLS or SCHED_ACT program that stores
__sk_buff->queue_mapping (a tc BPF action is enough), attach it to a
transmit qdisc (for example a matchall filter on a prio root), and send a
packet. With a 1-queue device a store of 1 indexes one past dev->_tx[].
Under KASAN with panic_on_warn=1 the unfixed kernel faults with "BUG:
KASAN: slab-out-
---truncated---

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: inherit FMODE_NONOTIFY when opening directory realfiles When fanotify hands a listener an fd for a…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: inherit FMODE_NONOTIFY when opening directory realfiles

When fanotify hands a listener an fd for a permission event on an
overlay directory, ovl_dir_open_realfile() opens the real directory via
dentry_open(), not backing_file_open(), so the lower open could still
raise FS_OPEN_PERM and deadlock a listener that also marks the backing
filesystem.

Export dentry_open_nonotify() and call it from ovl_path_open_realfile()
when the overlay user file must not generate events.  Ordinary
ovl_path_open() callers are unchanged.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: reject a negative TCP header offset in qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() stores…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: reject a negative TCP header offset in qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init()

qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() stores skb_transport_offset(), or the inner
offset, in the unsigned hdr_len. A header in front of skb->data gives a
negative offset. For an offset a little below zero, pskb_may_pull() gets a
small length and succeeds. Then a 64-bit kernel reads the TCP header far
after the skb and can crash. Further below zero pskb_may_pull() fails.

Commit 28a57fb2c5df ("net: iptunnel: fix stale transport header during
tunnel decapsulation") fixed one source of such offsets. Other code that
removes bytes from the front of a packet can leave the same stale header.

Return SKB_DROP_REASON_SKB_BAD_GSO for a negative offset in the TCP branch.
SKB_GSO_UDP_L4 and the other GSO types read no header and still get a wrong
qdisc_pkt_len(). On a 64-bit kernel only packets that cause the read after
the skb today get a new result. Then __dev_queue_xmit() drops them and
returns -EINVAL, but sch_handle_ingress() ignores the result. Their content
can be valid. Thus the code that leaves the header stale needs its own fix.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vhost/vsock: size receive SKBs from declared payload vhost_vsock_alloc_skb() sizes the skb from iov_length()…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vhost/vsock: size receive SKBs from declared payload

vhost_vsock_alloc_skb() sizes the skb from iov_length(), the total guest
descriptor length.  virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt() instead adds hdr->len to
rx_bytes and buf_used, and budgets each queued skb as SKB_TRUESIZE(0).  The
guest controls the descriptor length and hdr->len independently.

A guest can therefore provide a 64 KiB descriptor while declaring a zero
payload.  The descriptor-sized skb remains queued, rx_bytes and buf_used
remain unchanged, and only the fixed queue-entry budget limits retention.
This is not a lifetime leak: the skb is freed when dequeued or at socket
teardown.  Repeating this across connections can nevertheless exhaust host
memory.  On Linux v7.2, 455 such descriptors retained 30,255,680 bytes for
a 262,144-byte receive buffer; a full-payload control retained 265,984
bytes.

Vhost previously read hdr->len and allocated pkt->buf from that value.  The
conversion from virtio_vsock_pkt to sk_buff instead allocated receive skbs
from the descriptor length, introducing the allocation-accounting mismatch.

Copy the header into a stack object and validate hdr->len before allocating
the skb.  Size the allocation as sizeof(hdr) + payload_len so descriptor
capacity no longer determines queued memory.  Check payload_len against
len - sizeof(hdr) to avoid addition overflow on 32-bit hosts.

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mptcp: do not use Fast Open on MP_JOIN subflows tcp_fastopen_create_child() hands the SYN packet itself to…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mptcp: do not use Fast Open on MP_JOIN subflows

tcp_fastopen_create_child() hands the SYN packet itself to
subflow_syn_recv_sock(). For an MP_JOIN request this takes the
fatal fallback: the cloned child is destroyed and handed back with
drop_req flagged, but tcp_fastopen_create_child() does not check
the flag and queues it, so accept() can expose the freed child.

MP_JOIN cannot use Fast Open: data on a subflow requires the
completed HMAC exchange (RFC 8684, sec. 3.2). Refuse it (only the
TFO path passes a SYN skb here) and let tcp_conn_request() fall
back to the regular MP_JOIN handshake; also strip the Fast Open
cookie from MP_JOIN SYN/ACKs.

[ Moving code to avoid clearing TS and consolidating checks. ]

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: keep the CS user fence BO in GTT The CS ioctl hands the GPU the GART address of the user fence BO…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: keep the CS user fence BO in GTT

The CS ioctl hands the GPU the GART address of the user fence BO, but
since the BO keeps its own preferred and allowed domains, it no longer
makes sure the BO is in GTT. A user fence in a VRAM BO, which only needs
to be a page in size, gets its address from amdgpu_bo_gpu_offset(), which
warns about non-contiguous VRAM. On navi31, a CS with a user fence in a
4K VRAM BO, or in one created with AMDGPU_GEM_CREATE_VM_ALWAYS_VALID:

  WARNING: amdgpu_object.c:1531 at amdgpu_bo_gpu_offset+0x86/0xb0 [amdgpu], CPU#11: cs_gem_checks/18393
  RIP: 0010:amdgpu_bo_gpu_offset+0x86/0xb0 [amdgpu]
  Call Trace:
   <TASK>
   amdgpu_cs_parser_bos.isra.0+0x4eb/0x850 [amdgpu]
   amdgpu_cs_ioctl+0x97e/0x2510 [amdgpu]
   drm_ioctl_kernel+0xac/0x110 [drm]
   drm_ioctl+0x2c6/0x5b0 [drm]
   __x64_sys_ioctl+0xa0/0xf0
   do_syscall_64+0xa3/0x4d0
   entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x76/0x7e

and BOs which can't be in GTT at all, like GWS or OA ones of a page in
size, pass the checks as well.

Only take BOs which can't be anywhere else than in GTT as user fence,
which the CS then validates there along with its other BOs. While at it,
detect userptrs with amdgpu_ttm_tt_is_userptr(); amdgpu_ttm_tt_get_usermm()
returns NULL once the task which created the userptr is gone.

v2: only take BOs which can only be in GTT instead of special casing the
    user fence BO in the validation, use amdgpu_ttm_tt_is_userptr()
    (Christian)

(cherry picked from commit f16989def9561d04d0f2e77216f5319112d29bf1)

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdkfd: use the queue's process info for the WPTR BO eviction fence amdgpu_amdkfd_map_gtt_bo_to_gart()…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdkfd: use the queue's process info for the WPTR BO eviction fence

amdgpu_amdkfd_map_gtt_bo_to_gart() removes the eviction fence of
bo->vm_bo->vm->process_info from the WPTR BO of a new queue. bo->vm_bo
is the VM which opened the BO last, not necessarily the KFD process' VM,
and a render node VM has no process info.

On navi31, an unprivileged process which exports its WPTR BO with
AMDKFD_IOC_EXPORT_DMABUF and imports it on a second render node fd
oopses in AMDKFD_IOC_CREATE_QUEUE:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000060
  RIP: 0010:amdgpu_amdkfd_map_gtt_bo_to_gart+0x86/0x1a0 [amdgpu]
   init_user_queue.part.0+0x180/0x250 [amdgpu]
   pqm_create_queue+0x32d/0x730 [amdgpu]
   kfd_ioctl_create_queue+0x583/0x9f0 [amdgpu]

Pass the process info of the queue instead. With the fix, the queue is
created and destroyed normally.

(cherry picked from commit 6b4157498a176bd1c6083f6bb5aaf8a257a2027e)

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: check amdgpu_vm_ready() in dma-buf move notify amdgpu_dma_buf_move_notify() touches the page…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: check amdgpu_vm_ready() in dma-buf move notify

amdgpu_dma_buf_move_notify() touches the page tables without first
calling amdgpu_vm_ready(). When a process is SIGKILLed, its VM entities
are stopped. Teardown of an imported dma-buf then tries to clear PTEs by
submitting to one of those stopped entities. That eventually hangs the
task.

Commit aa5fc4362fac ("drm/amdgpu: fix task hang from failed job
submission during process kill") added the stopped entity check in
amdgpu_vm_ready() and used it in amdgpu_cs_vm_handling(). That did not
cover a call in amdgpu_dma_buf_move_notify(), what was already mentioned
in:
https://lists.freedesktop.org/archives/amd-gfx/2025-October/133076.html

Tested by SIGKILLing a GPU workload holding imported dma-bufs. Without
the patch "Trying to push to a killed entity" errors are logged, then a
task hangs. With the patch there are no hung tasks. This was tested on a
6.18 kernel.

(cherry picked from commit bee5c9d7a34cb1b510ad3b4c18c30f9d38b0ab7d)

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu/userq: validate the moved individual BOs on restore An individual BO of a user queue VM, i.e.
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu/userq: validate the moved individual BOs on restore

An individual BO of a user queue VM, i.e. one which doesn't share the
root reservation, goes to the individual needs_update list when it is
evicted. The user queue restore looked at vm->invalidated for them, which
the VM state machine rework turned into the always_valid evicted list and
commit 18decfc9e8cc ("drm/amdgpu/userq: actually validate userq BOs")
into the individual evicted one. That list only holds imported DMA-bufs of
compute VMs though, so for a user queue VM nothing is validated.

The restore then neither locks such a BO nor moves it back. Its PTEs are
updated to wherever it is now, cleared if it went to system memory, and
it doesn't get the new eviction fence, so it can move again under the
running queue.

On navi48, once the BOs of an SDMA user queue are evicted from GTT
(debugfs amdgpu_evict_gtt) the queue faults on its ring and rptr:

  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0:   in page starting at address 0x0000000100000000 from client 10
  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: 	 Faulty UTCL2 client ID: SDMA0 (0xd)
  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0:   in page starting at address 0x0000000100101000 from client 10

Validate the BOs on the individual needs_update list like before.

(cherry picked from commit eb0d94765d4be18d41e93ad09947dd9cc06ed31a)

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: clear RB_OVERFLOW bit when enabling interrupts for navi10_ih Port this change to navi10_ih.c…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: clear RB_OVERFLOW bit when enabling interrupts for navi10_ih

Port this change to navi10_ih.c:
commit afbf7955ff01 ("drm/amdgpu: clear RB_OVERFLOW bit when enabling interrupts")

Setting IH_RB_WPTR to 0 does not clear RB_OVERFLOW if RB_ENABLE is not
set. Pulse WPTR_OVERFLOW_CLEAR after RB_ENABLE (and with
WPTR_OVERFLOW_ENABLE) so overflow is cleared when interrupts are
enabled.

(cherry picked from commit 713fb4ab04f4d2af6120f8eb607c5673b2759b38)

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amd/display: Avoid closing unowned DDC pins [WHY] dal_ddc_open() cleans up pins it acquires on later…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amd/display: Avoid closing unowned DDC pins

[WHY]
dal_ddc_open() cleans up pins it acquires on later failures. If the
data-pin open fails, this attempt acquired nothing. If opening the
clock pin or configuring fails, dal_ddc_open() closes the pins it
opened. An extra dal_ddc_close() is unnecessary and unsafe:
GPIO_RESULT_ALREADY_OPENED can mean AUX owns the existing handles,
and closing them here would disrupt AUX.

[HOW]
Remove the extra dal_ddc_close() from the failed-open path.

(cherry picked from commit 175ae7772b68757b4932f34ff862923cab7abe21)

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu/gfx12: disallow GFXOFF while updating the SPM VMID gfx_v12_0_update_spm_vmid() does a…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu/gfx12: disallow GFXOFF while updating the SPM VMID

gfx_v12_0_update_spm_vmid() does a read-modify-write of RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL
over MMIO without keeping GFX powered, unlike gfx11. When GFX is in
GFXOFF at that point the update doesn't stick, and with the SPM VMID
programmed on submission again, the job of a process with a reserved
VMID can still run with the SPM writing through VMID 0.

On navi48, after a few other submissions and a VM fault on the same VM,
a COPY_DATA of RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL from such a job reads 0 although the
update was called for it:

  $ amd_uapi_regression --run-subtest cs-secure-ib-compute,gem-mapping-info-high-va,gpuvm-fault-high-va,reserved-vmid-spm-vmid
  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: [gfxhub] page fault (src_id:0 ring:40 vmid:7 pasid:185)
  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: 	 Faulty UTCL2 client ID: SDMA1 (0xe)
  RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL in the job: 0x00000000

With GFXOFF disallowed around the update it reads the reserved VMID 15.

(cherry picked from commit 907aebc5578ae09fa5c0e2f0784201295837e60b)

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amd/display: Fix NULL deref in dcn401_update_clocks_update_dtb_dto [Why]…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amd/display: Fix NULL deref in dcn401_update_clocks_update_dtb_dto

[Why]
resource_get_otg_master_for_stream() can return NULL if no OTG master pipe
is found for a given stream. The current code dereferences this pointer
without a NULL check. This may lead to a possible NULL pointer
dereference.

[How]
Add an explicit NULL check and skip the stream if the OTG master is not
found. This is similar to dcn60_update_clocks_update_dtb_dto().

Found by Linux Verification Center (linuxtesting.org) with SVACE.

(cherry picked from commit ffde3d74c1faeeb645b66d02d02fdae3e073941b)

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: Fix duplicate dependency fence releases drm_sched_job_add_dependency() consumes its fence…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: Fix duplicate dependency fence releases

drm_sched_job_add_dependency() consumes its fence reference on success
and failure. Do not release the fence again if
drm_sched_job_add_dependency() fails.

(cherry picked from commit e04f3dfb2071451633e6440a3911a9bb65df9144)

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: Report MES ring wait timeouts.
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: Report MES ring wait timeouts.

Return -ETIMEDOUT when the fence wait before submission expires instead
of reporting success without submitting the packet.

(cherry picked from commit 34341594a87b4a3f28be41e3e70a4787f02b3d9e)

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: Clamp the ATIF backlight curve to its 99 points amdgpu_atif_query_backlight_caps() stores the…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: Clamp the ATIF backlight curve to its 99 points

amdgpu_atif_query_backlight_caps() stores the firmware's number_of_points
as data_points but copies only the 99 points that luminance_data[] holds.
number_of_points is a u8, so a firmware table that claims more makes the
custom curve code in amdgpu_dm index past the array, and
dm_query_extended_brightness_caps() copy past the end of the
data_points[] buffer it fills

Clamp the count to ATIF_QBTC_MAX_DATA_POINTS and warn, since a table
that claims more is a firmware bug

(cherry picked from commit af8a1c2b7d3de4960e10f94e8ba2fc0ccd168072)

title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: drop the dma-buf reference when a KFD import fails import_obj_create() takes a reference on the…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: drop the dma-buf reference when a KFD import fails

import_obj_create() takes a reference on the dma-buf for the new kgd_mem,
